stories.headline: Trump Calls Jensen Huang Last-Minute to Join China Trip, Reviving Hopes for H200 Sales

key_facts.fact: Trump called Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on May 12 after seeing media coverage of his absence from the delegation, asking him to join the China trip
key_facts.excerpt: After seeing the media coverage of Huang's absence from the delegation, Trump called the Nvidia executive and asked him to join, a source familiar with the situation told CNBC.

key_facts.fact: Huang flew to Alaska to board Air Force One during the trip's refueling stopover, joining Trump's flight to Beijing
key_facts.excerpt: 'The president called Jensen this morning after seeing reports that he wasn't joining trip. Told him he wanted him to come. Jensen flew to Alaska to meet AF1,' a person familiar with the surprising sequence of events said Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: Huang did not appear on an initial White House list of executives, which included Tesla's Elon Musk and Apple's Tim Cook
key_facts.excerpt: Huang did not appear on an initial list of executives provided by the White House earlier this week, which included Tesla CEO Elon Musk and Apple's Tim Cook.

key_facts.fact: Huang's late addition is fueling hopes in China for a deal on Nvidia's stalled effort to sell H200 AI chips to local customers
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will join President Donald Trump during his visit to Beijing, igniting hopes in China that the trip could yield results in the tech giant's long-stalled effort to sell its powerful H200 AI chips to local customers.

key_facts.fact: Trump posted on Truth Social that he will ask President Xi to 'open up' China for U.S. businesses as his 'first request' during the summit
key_facts.excerpt: I will be asking President Xi, a Leader of extraordinary distinction, to 'open up' China so that these brilliant people can work their magic, and help bring the People's Republic to an even higher level!

key_facts.fact: Huang has previously pegged China's market for AI chips at $50 billion and told CNBC last week it 'would be a privilege' to accompany Trump
key_facts.excerpt: Huang, who's pegged China's market for AI chips at $50 billion, told CNBC last week that 'it would be a privilege' to accompany Trump on the trip.

stories.headline: Anduril Raises $5B Series H at $61B Valuation, Doubling Year-Ago Value, May IPO in 2027

key_facts.fact: Anduril raised a $5B Series H led by Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz at a $61B valuation
key_facts.excerpt: Anduril raised a $5B Series H led by Thrive and a16z at a $61B valuation, up from $30.5B in June 2025, taking its total funding to $6.82B, and may IPO in 2027

key_facts.fact: The valuation doubled from $30.5B in June 2025, and total funding to date now stands at $6.82B
key_facts.excerpt: up from $30.5B in June 2025, taking its total funding to $6.82B, and may IPO in 2027

key_facts.fact: The company makes A.I.-backed weapons and may pursue an IPO in 2027
key_facts.excerpt: The start-up, which makes A.I.-backed weapons, was valued at $61 billion in the financing round, double what it was a year ago.

key_facts.fact: Lux Capital and Founders Fund also participated as existing investors in the multibillion-dollar round
key_facts.excerpt: Lux Capital and Founders Fund are also expected to participate.

key_facts.fact: Anduril, founded in 2017 by Palmer Luckey, develops AI-powered hardware and software for autonomous defense systems including drones and surveillance platforms
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2017 by tech entrepreneur Palmer Luckey, Anduril develops AI-powered hardware and software for autonomous defence systems, including drones and surveillance platforms used by the US government.

stories.headline: xAI Added 19 Gas Turbines to Colossus 2 in Past Two Months Despite Clean Air Act Lawsuit

key_facts.fact: Internal emails show xAI added 19 natural gas turbines at its Colossus 2 data center campus in Southhaven, Mississippi over the past two months
key_facts.excerpt: xAI has added 19 natural gas turbines to its second data center campus in Southhaven, Mississippi, over the past two months, according to internal emails seen by WIRED.

key_facts.fact: xAI is fighting a lawsuit filed by NAACP in April alleging Clean Air Act violations from operating unpermitted gas turbines
key_facts.excerpt: On Tuesday, NAACP sued xAI and its subsidiary, MZX Tech, for the tech companies' unlawful operation of dozens of unpermitted methane gas turbines to power its Colossus 2 data center in South Memphis.

key_facts.fact: The original NAACP complaint cited 27 unpermitted gas turbines with 495 MW of generating capacity
key_facts.excerpt: The lawsuit explains that xAI is illegally operating 27 gas turbines without an air permit in Southaven, Mississippi, effectively building a power plant for its Colossus 2 data center, which powers the company's chatbot, Grok.

key_facts.fact: A May 6 preliminary injunction filing claims up to 33 unpermitted gas turbines are now at the site, with only 14 equipped with emission controls
key_facts.excerpt: lawsuit claims six [...] unpermitted gas turbines up to 33. According to the lawsuit, of those 33 [...] only 14 are equipped with emission controls.

key_facts.fact: The Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality approved a Prevention of Significant Deterioration permit for 41 turbines at the site in March
key_facts.excerpt: In March, the MDEQ approved a Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD) permit for 41 turbines at the site.

stories.headline: NAND Contract Prices Up 600%+ and DRAM Up ~400% Since Late September 2025 on AI Buildout

key_facts.fact: Contract prices for NAND chips are up 600%+ since late September 2025, while DRAM contract prices are up ~400%, with analysts expecting further gains
key_facts.excerpt: Analysis: contract prices for NAND chips are up 600%+ since late September 2025, while those for DRAM chips are up ~400%, with analysts expecting further gains

key_facts.fact: Bernstein analyst Mark Li reported overall DRAM contract prices in April were 57% higher versus Q1, with server DRAM up 48%, mobile up ~80%, and consumer up ~60%
key_facts.excerpt: Analyst Mark Li stated in a note to clients that overall DRAM contract prices in April were 57% higher versus the first quarter, with server DRAM up 48%, mobile up roughly 80%, and consumer up approximately 60%.

key_facts.fact: NAND contract prices are indicated to rise 65-70% quarter-on-quarter in 2Q 2026, driven primarily by SSD and mobile NAND packages
key_facts.excerpt: NAND contract prices are indicated to rise 65%-70% quarter-on-quarter, driven primarily by SSD and mobile NAND packages.

key_facts.fact: TrendForce projects PC DDR5 DRAM prices to rise 43-48% in Q2 2026, while DDR4 prices are expected to rise 35-40%
key_facts.excerpt: Market researcher TrendForce said on April 30 that PC DDR5 DRAM prices are projected to increase 43% to 48% in the second quarter, a 3 percentage-point upward revision from its previous forecast.

key_facts.fact: Bernstein flagged spot prices sent mixed signals — server DDR5 module spot prices down 6.7% MoM and NAND wafer spot prices fell ~7% as OEMs reduce purchases
key_facts.excerpt: However, Bernstein flagged that spot prices sent a more mixed signal, with server DDR5 module spot prices down 6.7% month-on-month and NAND wafer spot prices falling roughly 7%, as price increases weigh on consumer end demand and force OEMs and module houses to reduce purchases.

key_facts.fact: Demand for server DRAM and eSSD remains robust, keeping supply tight, but price increases are expected to decelerate notably into Q3 2026
key_facts.excerpt: demand remained robust for server DRAM and eSSD, and continued keeping supply tight... Price increases are expected to decelerate notably into the third quarter.

stories.headline: Samsung Pay Talks Collapse After 17 Hours; 50,000+ Workers Set to Strike May 21 for 18 Days

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics and its largest union failed to reach a pay deal after more than 17 hours of marathon talks that ended early Wednesday May 13
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics and its union failed to reach an agreement on the source of funds for performance bonuses and their institutionalization after more than 17 hours of marathon negotiations at the National Labor Relations Commission that lasted until the early morning of May 13.

key_facts.fact: More than 50,000 unionized workers are expected to strike for 18 days starting May 21, threatening AI chip production
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics and its South Korean labor union failed to reach a pay deal on Wednesday, its union leader said, expecting over 50,000 workers would go ahead with a full strike that threatens to disrupt production of AI and other chips.

key_facts.fact: The union demands the abolition of the 50%-of-base-salary cap on bonus pay and the allocation of 15% of annual operating profit to the bonus pool
key_facts.excerpt: The union has called for the scrapping of a cap on bonus pay currently set at 50 per cent of annual base salary, the allocation of 15 per cent of annual operating profit to bonus pay and more clarity on how bonus pay is calculated.

key_facts.fact: South Korean Prime Minister Kim Min-seok called an emergency meeting of related ministers, citing the 'gravity of the impact on the national economy'
key_facts.excerpt: Underscoring the angst caused by the potential strike, South Korea called an emergency meeting for related ministers. There, Prime Minister Kim Min-seok instructed the government to closely manage the situation 'considering the gravity of the impact on the national economy'.

key_facts.fact: A walkout could delay shipments to customers, push up chip prices further and benefit rivals such as SK Hynix
key_facts.excerpt: More than 50,000 workers could walk off [...] a move that would likely delay shipments to customers, push up chip prices further and benefit rivals.

key_facts.fact: The union grievance centers on the bonus gap with rival SK Hynix; union representative Choi Seung-ho said no agenda items were addressed
key_facts.excerpt: I would like to express some regret that none of the agenda items requested by the union have been addressed,' union representative Choi Seung-ho told reporters at about 3 a.m. local time on Wednesday.

stories.headline: Foxconn Confirms Cyberattack on North American Factories; Nitrogen Ransomware Claims 8TB Theft

key_facts.fact: Foxconn confirmed Tuesday May 12 that some of its North American factories suffered a cyberattack and affected facilities are resuming normal production
key_facts.excerpt: Some of Foxconn's factories in North America suffered a cyberattack,' a Foxconn spokesperson told The Register. 'The cybersecurity team immediately activated the response mechanism and implemented multiple operational measures to ensure the continuity of production and delivery.'

key_facts.fact: The Nitrogen ransomware group claimed to have stolen 8 TB of data and more than 11 million files from Foxconn
key_facts.excerpt: Nitrogen ransomware criminals on Monday claimed to have breached the Taiwan-based company and stolen 8 TB of data comprising more than 11 million files.

key_facts.fact: Nitrogen claims the leaks include confidential instructions, project documentation, and technical drawings tied to Intel, Apple, Google, Dell, AMD and Nvidia projects
key_facts.excerpt: 'These include files such as confidential instructions, projects, and drawings from Intel, Apple, Google, Dell, Nvidia, and many other projects,' reads the group's announcement.

key_facts.fact: The Wisconsin Mount Pleasant facility began experiencing Wi-Fi issues May 1 and core plant infrastructure was disrupted; production was interrupted for roughly a week
key_facts.excerpt: Per The Cybersec Guru, the facility's network began experiencing issues on May 1, with Wi-Fi being cut off at 7 AM ET, and disruptions to the core plant infrastructure occurring by 11 AM ET. Manufacturing seemingly remained affected until May 12, 2026.

key_facts.fact: Foxconn operates factories in Wisconsin, Ohio, Texas, Virginia, Indiana and several locations across Mexico; the company declined to specify how many were impacted
key_facts.excerpt: A spokesperson for the company confirmed the incident but declined to provide specifics on how many factories in North America were impacted. Foxconn has factories in Wisconsin, Ohio, Texas, Virginia, Indiana and several across Mexico.

key_facts.fact: Nitrogen, active since 2023, is believed to use code derived from the leaked Conti 2 builder and follows a double-extortion model
key_facts.excerpt: Nitrogen, which has been around since 2023, is believed to be one of the various ransomware offshoots that borrowed code from the leaked Conti 2 builder.

stories.headline: Photonic Closes $200M+ Round at $2B Valuation, Backed by Mubadala, Microsoft, RBC, Bell

key_facts.fact: Vancouver-based quantum computing startup Photonic announced the final close of over $200M USD ($275M CAD) in funding, hitting a $2B USD post-money valuation
key_facts.excerpt: Photonic, Inc., a Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada-based developer of distributed quantum computing infrastructure, raised over $200m USD ($275m CAD) in funding, achieving a $2 billion USD post-money valuation.

key_facts.fact: The round was led by UK-based sustainable technology firm Planet First Partners, with new investors BDC, Export Development Canada, Bell Ventures, Firgun Ventures, and InBC Investment Corp
key_facts.excerpt: The round was led by Planet First Partners, with participation from new investors BDC, EDC, Bell Ventures, Firgun Ventures, and InBC Investment Corp., alongside returning investors Mubadala Capital, RBC, TELUS, BCI, and Microsoft.

key_facts.fact: Photonic added $70M to its initial $130M January raise to complete the financing, bringing total capital raised to over $350M USD
key_facts.excerpt: Vancouver-based quantum computing startup Photonic raised an additional $70M after a $130M raise announced in January, giving it a $2B post-money valuation

key_facts.fact: Photonic's 'Entanglement First' architecture uses optically-linked silicon spin qubits, allowing fault-tolerant quantum systems to scale over existing fiber and telecom infrastructure
key_facts.excerpt: Photonic Inc. develops an 'Entanglement First™ Architecture' that utilizes optically-linked silicon spin qubits. This design combines silicon-based qubits with native photonic connectivity, enabling fault-tolerant quantum computing systems to scale seamlessly over existing global fiber and telecom infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: Other backers include the UK government's National Security Strategic Investment Fund and Canadian financiers Inovia Capital and Yaletown Partners
key_facts.excerpt: Other investors include the U.K. government's National Security Strategic Investment Fund and Canadian financiers Inovia Capital and Yaletown Partners. Photonic has raised more than US$350-million.

key_facts.fact: Photonic has more than 160 employees and is led by former video game executive Don Mattrick, with previous CEO Paul Terry moving to chief product officer
key_facts.excerpt: He's since moved to chief product officer, with longtime video game executive Don Mattrick taking over the top job.
